PhonePe._comment:
Pune site, one counter: welcome_drink x2, soup, bread, rice, dal, veg_dry, veg_gravy, nonveg_main x3, plus the const white_rice and papad. The sheet lists 47 lines and MOST OF THEM ARE ALREADY THE CITY'S: Pune's ruleset carries the 10-day-plus item cooldown, no-repeat-within-the-horizon, the monthly week-signature cooldown, colour diversity at three distinct / max two alike, premium gravy and premium veg dry weekly, kabuli chana weekly, kofta weekly plus a 14-day window, mix-veg-or-aloo-dry at least weekly, pappu dal weekly, yellow dal at least twice, oil-based bread monthly, leafy veg dry once in 15 days and plain chapati repeatable. Restating any of them here would be a second copy to keep in step, so only the delta is below. Three of the remaining lines are inert against Pune's list and are deliberately NOT written — see the bottom of this comment.

WHAT THE SHEET ASKS FOR THAT THIS COUNTER CANNOT DO YET, because the slot does not exist on the row: the Mon/Wed/Fri salad and Tue/Thu chaat swap (no salad slot, and no city carries a `chaat` course_type at all); everything about sweets — ice cream monthly, no repeat in 15 days, no milk-based, premium sweet three days, dessert form not repeating (no dessert slot); the pulao-then-raita / otherwise-curd pairing and the Mon/Wed/Fri curd staple (no curd_side slot); and the starter rules — deep-fried after a rice bread, veg starter under veg dry, chutney with an Indian starter (no starter slot).

NOT WRITTEN BECAUSE THEY WOULD MATCH NOTHING: 'if Bread is a rice-bread then Rice must be a liquid rice' (Pune's bread pool holds no rice bread) and 'veg gravy and flavoured rice must complement, spicy to mellow' (`is_mellow` is 0 on every Pune veg gravy). A rule whose selector matches nothing loads as zero rules while /plan still answers 200 — see note 9 — so they are recorded here rather than shipped inert.

TWO DATA GAPS, both flagged in docs/pending_config_changes.md: Pune carries no `boiled_egg` and no `boiled_chicken` row, so the two staple non-veg pins below print as text instead of being solved; and it carries one buttermilk row and no masala buttermilk, so 'plain buttermilk Mon/Wed/Fri, masala buttermilk Tue/Thu, both staple' cannot be written at all.

rules._comment: 'noveg 1 will serve chicken gravy on mon,wed,frid and egg gravy on tue and tursday.' The first non-veg cell only — the other two are the boiled staples pinned below. Pune carries 124 chicken gravies and 5 egg gravies; a component RELAXES rather than failing, so a week where the egg gravies are all cooled down degrades to whatever the pool can supply instead of going INFEASIBLE, and says so in the explanation.
rules.name: phonepe_nonveg_1_by_weekday

rules._comment: 'indian bread will serve chapati as staple on mon,wed and fri . Then tue and thur will serve paratas'. The sheet's other wording, '3 days Chapati and 3 days Paratha', adds to six over a five-day week; the weekday split is the one that is actionable and it is what the sample grid prints (Chapati / Ajwain Paratha / Chapati / Plain Paratha / Chapati). Pune has 10 plain chapatti/phulka rows and 14 parathas across `flavoured_paratha`, `tandoor` and `thepla`.
rules.name: phonepe_bread_by_weekday

rules._comment:
'3 days rice 2 day pulao'. Stated as the pulao half only, because the other three days are then whatever the rice slot picks that is not a pulao — two rules would be two things to keep in step. `exact` over the horizon rather than `max_per_week`, since the client gave a count and not a cap.

Selected by FLAG OR NAME, and the name is doing most of the work: `is_pulao` is set on 10 of Pune's 110 rices while 47 of them are pulaos, so the flag alone let the solver serve three pulaos in a week and still report the rule satisfied — measured, on the first plan this file produced. Every one of the 47 the name catches is a real pulao, so the union is safe as well as accurate, and it leaves the flag in place for a row whose name does not say so.
rules.name: phonepe_pulao_2x

rules._comment: '2 Days Paneer in week' — the total, across both veg slots, which is why this one has no `base_slot`. The gravy half is the rule below.
rules.name: phonepe_paneer_2x_total

rules._comment: 'pannar in gravy weekly once'. One of the two paneer days above is the gravy; the other is free to be the veg dry. Both numbers are the client's and they are consistent, so both are written rather than picking one.
rules.name: phonepe_paneer_gravy_1x

rules._comment: 'All black dals together: max once/week.' Three Pune dals carry `is_black_dal`; the city ruleset caps black CHANA gravies but says nothing about the dal, so this is a real addition rather than a restatement.
rules.name: phonepe_black_dal_weekly

rules._comment: 'Flavour Rice and Veg Gravy should not be the same color on the same day.' The sheet's '(except on Chinese day if allowed)' has nothing to except: PhonePe's theme map is north on four days and mix on Thursday, with no Chinese day.
rules.name: phonepe_rice_and_gravy_differ_in_colour

rules._comment: 'Welcome drink colors cannot repeat on consecutive days.' Bangalore runs the same rule city-wide; Pune does not, and PhonePe is the first Pune counter with two drink cells.
rules.name: phonepe_welcome_drink_no_repeat_colour

rules._comment: 'Welcome drink 1 is non dairy' — as a per-day cap across the two cells, which is what it amounts to on a counter whose other drink is meant to be the buttermilk. Written this way because a composition cannot target one cell of a slot, and it is worth writing rather than assuming: the first plan this file produced put `masala_milk` in a drink cell on Wednesday. Dairy is matched by flag OR name — `drink_rule_group` cannot be trusted for it, since Pune files `masala_milk` and `badam_milk` as `fruit_drink`. The pair catches 10 of 39, which is the lassis, the milks, taak and the buttermilk.
rules.name: phonepe_welcome_drink_max_one_dairy

constant_items._comment: 'Non Veg 2 & 3 will serve Boiled egg and boiled chicken daily as staple' — the same dish every day, so pins rather than rules. Indexed so the FIRST non-veg cell still solves and keeps its weekday composition above. Pune carries neither dish today, so both are stamped as text post-solve and are invisible to colour, variety and cooldown; add a `boiled_egg` and a `boiled_chicken` row to the Pune list and the same pins start being solved instead, with no config change.
